cells.tense: You're building, right now, with your hands on it.
cells.verb: raising something new out of what fell away
cells.place: right where you decide this and not that
cells.ask: You could show one person how you're doing it — not the finished thing, the way of working — and let the showing be the next thing you build.
cells.core:
You're building, right now, with your hands on it. Something that was in the way came down, and instead of standing in the rubble you've started putting up what can only stand there now — and you're choosing each piece, not just stacking what's near. The work isn't fighting you. It goes at the pace the material allows, and you're not alone in it even on the days you work alone.

This is a working balance, not a finish line. What it's free to feed next is somebody else's hands: you could show one person how you're doing it — not the finished thing, the way of working — and let the showing be the next thing you build.
cells.sheetLine: You're choosing what gets built, and building it.

cells.tense: You're building against a future that hasn't agreed to anything.
cells.verb: raising something new out of what fell away
cells.place: right where you decide this and not that
cells.ask: You could walk toward the people this is for and ask what they actually need to belong in it — and take down one piece that's only there to make you feel sure.
cells.core:
You're building against a future that hasn't agreed to anything. Something came down, and the open ground is making you nervous, so you're putting up walls fast — deciding, deciding, deciding — before anyone else has had a say in what goes there. The more you decide, the less room there is for the thing to turn out better than your plan.

The way back isn't to stop building. It's to find out what's being built for. You could walk toward the people this is for and ask what they actually need to belong in it — and take down one piece that's only there to make you feel sure. What comes back is a structure that stands because it's true, not because you braced it.
cells.sheetLine: You're deciding faster than anyone asked you to.

cells.tense: You're still standing at what fell, and the building hasn't started.
cells.verb: raising something new out of what fell away
cells.place: right where you decide this and not that
cells.ask: You could make one clear call that someone else can rely on — a small, reliable yes or no — and let that steadiness pull the first stone into place.
cells.core:
You're still standing at what fell, and the building hasn't started. The clearing happened — you saw it, you may even have wanted it — but the ground stayed open, and choosing a direction has started to feel like something other people do. There's room here for something new. Nothing is going up.

Don't try to want it harder; that won't move. The way through is to be dependable about one thing, anywhere. You could make one clear call that someone else can rely on — a small, reliable yes or no — and let that steadiness pull the first stone into place. What comes back is a direction that starts from what you actually saw when the old thing came down.
cells.sheetLine: The ground's clear. You haven't picked up a stone.

cells.tense: You're already building, and you're calling it the way things turned out.
cells.verb: raising something new out of what fell away
cells.place: right where you decide this and not that
cells.ask: You could say, once, 'I chose this' — and the next time someone leans on it, hold it, instead of letting it be just how it happened.
cells.core:
You're already building, and you're calling it the way things turned out. Something fell, and what's going up in its place has your decisions all through it — this, not that, every day — but you'd describe it as circumstance, or momentum, or what everyone agreed to. The direction is being set. The one setting it isn't signing.

The way back is smaller than it sounds. You could say, once, 'I chose this' — and the next time someone leans on it, hold it, instead of letting it be just how it happened. What comes back is a build that knows what it's for, because the one choosing it finally does.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering this. You keep calling it drift.
